In an extensive interview with Joanna Stern, OpenAI President Greg Brockman discusses the company's recent changes to the ChatGPT desktop app and its plans for a tabless interface. Watch the interview below.

Work could soon seamlessly operate within ChatGPT

A few days ago, Joanna Stern released a teaser on her newly launched YouTube channel, New Things, for an upcoming interview with OpenAI President Greg Brockman.

Today, Stern released the full interview, covering topics such as the new ChatGPT Voice, OpenAI's hardware ambitions, the Apple lawsuit, and the recent Hugging Face breach.

During the interview, Stern mentions OpenAI's recent decision to merge the ChatGPT and Codex desktop apps, along with the launch of ChatGPT's new agent mode, Work.

The merged interface has left users confused, especially those who just want to continue using ChatGPT but struggle to find their chat history.

OpenAI subsequently updated the app, adding separate Work and ChatGPT tabs at the top of the interface, and adding a dropdown menu in the left panel to switch between ChatGPT and Codex. While the app is less difficult to use than before, it is still a little confusing.

When asked about this misstep, Brockman agreed with Stern's description of the new interface as "a little chaotic" and added that this is an "incremental step toward the future," where the Work tab will eventually disappear, with its functions "seamlessly integrating into ChatGPT."

Brockman also said that despite the confusing rollout of the merged app, OpenAI is still seeing the expected results, with the number of Codex users growing from 5 million to 10 million in just a few days.

When pressed on whether this growth is purely because Codex was "forced" into the ChatGPT app, Brockman acknowledged it once again, while also arguing that this was part of the intent:

The full interview is quite interesting and definitely worth a watch. There's also a very "Joanna Stern-style" attempt to add ChatGPT Voice to the conversation, which works about as well as you might imagine.
